findings.subject: Fixed warmup is not established convergence

findings.recommendation: Report the fixed 24-round warmup and per-process medians/spread. Do not call the measurements converged steady-state or intrinsic language/compiler costs; no extra measurement is required for the narrower report.

resolution.detail: Final text explicitly says fixed warmup did not establish steady state, preserves all samples and gives numeric drift/outlier evidence; no further measurement or source edit requested.

assessment: Controls support an honest bounded comparison of these concrete implementations. No normal-input correctness or unfair-transport blocker was found. KMP improves on the regex/split native baseline in small/header-heavy workloads but remains slower than the optimized-native scanner. Large-body ratios near one do not demonstrate a meaningful user-visible benefit.
publicationLimits: Performance samples are host JDK 17 observations, not Android ART or physical-device timing. Supplementary ART parser correctness is separately verified in the explicitly reported API 24 and API 37 scopes.
Native C++ and JNI string/array allocations are excluded from JVM thread allocation counts; no total-memory ranking.
C++ ranges and optimized native trim before substring allocation; current KMP returns raw header strings. These represent API/implementation choices, not unavoidable language overhead.
Each implementation runs in shared-process randomized balanced rounds; three fresh JVMs provide repeat observations, not independent deployments or universal confidence.
Input/source creation is outside measurement; full parser body draining and callbacks remain inside. No network, app-startup, rendering or whole-app memory conclusion.
Final progress values and exceptions are tested; intermediate wall-clock-throttled progress callback counts/timing are not compared.
